name: Australia

legalSystem.note: Federal common law system. The Commonwealth Parliament legislates for the matters this index measures, and the Federal Register of Legislation publishes an authorised consolidated compilation of every Act and legislative instrument in force. A compilation states its own compilation date on its first page, so the date a row reports is evidenced by the document rather than asserted. State and Territory law exists and is not on this register; where an indicator turns on it, that is a gap this profile does not close.

languageNote: Commonwealth law is enacted and published in English only.

instrumentTypes.note: The principal instrument. Cited by short title and section, e.g. Privacy Act 1988, s 6. The register serves the consolidated compilation, so the section as it now stands is directly citable.
Made under an Act, registered on the Federal Register, and disallowable by Parliament. Where an Act says the regulations may prescribe something, the operative rule is here.

Registered but not disallowable: guidelines, standards and determinations that bind the parties they are issued to. Legal texts published by government, so recordable as evidence; whether one controls an indicator is decided case by case.
OAIC Australian Privacy Principles guidelines, ACCC guidance and the like. Evidence of how a regulator reads a binding instrument, never the source of an obligation on their own.

portals.name: Federal Register of Legislation

collections.listing: Titles where collection is Act and isInForce is true
Titles where collection is LegislativeInstrument and isInForce is true
Titles where collection is NotifiableInstrument and isInForce is true

portals.notes: Publishes a public OData v4 API, so the register is enumerated rather than scraped. The API host sets no robots rules and answers immediately; the www host asks for a 10 second crawl delay, and that is where the cost of reading a document sits. Two quirks measured on 7 September 2026: the API refuses a filter of three conjoined clauses, so isPrincipal is applied to the rows after they arrive; and the /latest/text page is a single-page-application shell whose only useful content is its links into the EPUB text, which is the authored XHTML the register's own table of contents links to.

portals.name: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner
portals.notes: Registered privacy codes, and the Australian Privacy Principles guidelines that state how the Privacy Act's principles are read. The codes register is the part that carries binding instruments.

portals.name: Australian Communications and Media Authority
portals.notes: The register of telecommunications industry codes and standards. A registered industry code binds carriers by force of the Telecommunications Act, so it is law even though it is not an Act.

portals.name: Australian Prudential Regulation Authority
portals.notes: Prudential standards, CPS 234 on information security among them, which bind regulated financial entities. Most are also registered as legislative instruments, so the Federal Register carries them too.

portals.name: Australian Competition and Consumer Commission
portals.notes: Competition and consumer enforcement, and the Consumer Data Right rules made under the Competition and Consumer Act.

portals.name: IP Australia
portals.notes: Patents, trade marks and designs administration. The statutes themselves are on the Federal Register.

portals.name: Australian Border Force
portals.notes: Customs procedure and the electronic lodgement systems the trade facilitation pillars turn on.

portals.name: Foreign Investment Review Board
portals.notes: Guidance notes on the foreign investment screening regime. The Act and Regulations behind them are on the Federal Register.

portals.name: Australian Signals Directorate
portals.notes: The Information Security Manual and the Essential Eight. Advisory in form, but referenced by binding instruments made under the Security of Critical Infrastructure Act.

portals.name: .au Domain Administration
portals.notes: The .au licensing rules, which are the eligibility requirements for a domain name. Not a government host, which is why it is recorded as a registry rather than a regulator: a row citing it has to say what makes it authoritative.

commitments.name: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership

notes: Australia is the second economy built, and it is the easy one: the register enumerates itself through an API, the text is authored XHTML from one drafting template, and there is no non-English source path. It is the honest test of whether the pipeline is economy-generic, because nothing in it resembles Singapore's portal.

name: Malaysia

legalSystem.note: Common law inherited from England, alongside Syariah law in matters of personal status and a separate body of Sabah and Sarawak state law. Federal Acts are consolidated and reprinted by the Commissioner of Law Revision, and each reprint states on its cover the date it is current to. Subsidiary legislation is made as P.U. (A) and P.U. (B) instruments and is published separately from the Acts.

languageNote: Bahasa Melayu is the authoritative language of the law. The Laws of Malaysia portal publishes each Act in both a Malay and an English edition, and the English edition is a translation whose authority is subordinate: where the two differ, the Malay text governs. The register records which edition a document came from, so a row that quotes the English text is quoting a translation and says so.

instrumentTypes.note: The principal instrument, numbered in one series: Act 709 is the Personal Data Protection Act 2010. Cited by act number and section.
Regulations, rules and orders made under an Act. Where an Act leaves a standard to be prescribed, the standard is here.

instrumentTypes.localName: Notification, P.U. (B), and regulator policy documents
instrumentTypes.note: Bank Negara policy documents and MCMC determinations bind the licensees they are issued to by force of the parent Act. This is the tier v1 collapsed into the one above, scoring central bank guidance as though it were an Act.
Personal Data Protection Department guidance and similar. Evidence of how a regulator reads a binding instrument, never the source of an obligation on their own.

portals.name: Laws of Malaysia
portals.authority: Attorney General's Chambers, Commissioner of Law Revision
portals.notes: The portal's table of current principal Acts is published as a PDF it generates itself, and that PDF carries every Act's number, English title, consolidation date, and a link straight to the Act's own file. That is the register, taken from one official artefact. It is deliberately not taken from the portal's search feed, which now answers with an encrypted payload the page decrypts using a key it ships to the browser: reading that would make the register depend on a key one rotation away from silently returning nothing, which is how a predecessor of this system quietly stopped enumerating Malaysia altogether. Subsidiary legislation is not reachable this way -- its links are signed with a digest we cannot compute -- and is recorded as an open gap rather than a quiet absence.

portals.name: Personal Data Protection Department
portals.notes: The Act's subsidiary regulations and the sectoral codes of practice registered under it, which is where the operative detail of Malaysia's data protection regime sits. The pages that carry the codes are built client-side, so nothing is reachable by following links; the site runs WordPress and advertises its own read-only API, and the whole document library is enumerable through it. Uploads are filed under filename slugs, so a code enters the register under a provisional title and takes its real one from the first page of the document.

portals.name: Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission
portals.notes: Determinations, guidelines and the Content Code made under the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998. Binding on licensees through standard licence conditions rather than on their own terms, so a row citing one has to say what makes it binding.

portals.name: National Cyber Security Agency
portals.notes: The Cyber Security Act 2024 and the codes of practice for national critical information infrastructure entities made under it.

portals.name: Bank Negara Malaysia
portals.notes: Policy documents, the technology risk management one among them, binding on financial institutions. A policy document is not an Act, and treating it as one is a mistake this profile's instrument ranking exists to prevent.

portals.name: Royal Malaysian Customs Department
portals.notes: Customs procedure and the electronic declaration systems the trade facilitation pillars turn on. Publishes in Malay by default.

portals.name: Malaysian Investment Development Authority
portals.notes: Investment guidelines and the equity conditions attached to manufacturing and services licences.

portals.name: Intellectual Property Corporation of Malaysia
portals.notes: Patents, trade marks and copyright administration. Recorded as a lead rather than crawled: the site refused an automated client on every path tried by a predecessor of this system, and Malaysia's intellectual property statutes are on the Laws of Malaysia portal in any case.

portals.name: MYNIC
portals.notes: The .my registry's own eligibility policies, which are the domain name requirements. Not a government host, so a row citing it has to say what makes it authoritative.

commitments.name: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership

notes: Malaysia is the third economy built and the hardest of the three: no API, the law served as PDFs, an authoritative language that is not English, and a statute book whose subsidiary legislation is not enumerable from the portal. It is where the non-English source path is tested for real.

name: Singapore

legalSystem.note: English common law tradition. Statute is consolidated and kept current on Singapore Statutes Online, so the in-force text of an Act is directly citable and no separate consolidation step is needed. Subsidiary legislation made under an Act is published alongside it. Regulators additionally issue Notices and Directions that bind their licensees and Advisory Guidelines that do not.

languageNote: Malay is the national language, but legislation is enacted and published in English, and the English text is authoritative. A Singapore run therefore exercises no non-English source path; Malaysia is where that is tested.

instrumentTypes.note: The principal instrument. Cited by short title and section, e.g. Personal Data Protection Act 2012, s 26.
Made under an Act and published under it on SSO. Where the Act prescribes 'requirements prescribed under this Act', the operative rule usually lives here rather than in the Act.

instrumentTypes.localName: Notice or Direction issued by a regulator
instrumentTypes.note: MAS Notices, IMDA Directions, CSA Codes of Practice for CII owners. Binding on the entities they are issued to, and legal texts published by a government body, so recordable as evidence. Whether one is controlling for a given indicator is decided case by case.
PDPC Advisory Guidelines and MAS Guidelines state how a regulator reads a binding instrument. Evidence of interpretation, never the source of an obligation on their own.

portals.name: Singapore Statutes Online
portals.notes: Serves the in-force consolidated text. A document page carries only its first few provisions; the rest are requested by provision id, which the adapter does in one further request per instrument. robots.txt disallows /search and asks for a 6 second crawl delay; both are honoured, and discovery uses the browse listings rather than the search box.

portals.name: Singapore Government e-Gazette
portals.notes: Where commencement notifications and instruments not yet consolidated into SSO appear. Not crawled: SSO already carries the in-force text, and the gazette is the place to check a commencement date rather than to discover an instrument.

portals.name: Personal Data Protection Commission
portals.notes: Advisory Guidelines on the PDPA, and the enforcement decisions that make pillar 7 answerable in practice rather than on paper.

portals.name: Infocomm Media Development Authority
portals.notes: Telecommunications and media licensing, the Telecom Competition Code, and the electronic transactions regime.

portals.name: Monetary Authority of Singapore
portals.notes: MAS Notices bind financial institutions and are where sector-specific data and outsourcing requirements live. A cancelled Notice is a trap ESCAP's reviewers have flagged, so status must be read from the document.

portals.name: Cyber Security Agency of Singapore
portals.notes: Codes of Practice for critical information infrastructure owners under the Cybersecurity Act 2018.

portals.name: Singapore Customs
portals.notes: Customs procedure, the Networked Trade Platform, and the paperless trade commitments pillar 3 turns on.

portals.name: Intellectual Property Office of Singapore
portals.notes: Patents, trade marks, copyright and trade secrets administration.

portals.name: Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore
portals.notes: Competition enforcement and the consumer protection framework.

commitments.name: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership

notes: Singapore is the first economy built because ESCAP's own Round 1 database answers all 61 indicators for it, which makes the pillar 6 and 7 gate checkable against their sheet rather than against our own opinion.
